A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fun3DU and contain readable main papers and complete supplementary material. Visual inspection and page-image comparison support a reliable comparison despite the lack of extractable text.

before.justification: v4 reports original SceneFun3D segmentation experiments, baseline comparisons, ablations, runtime measurements, and qualitative results in the main paper and supplement.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark tables and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 corrects the specified view-selection computation: Equation (2) replaces D_KL with 1 - D_KL for both distance and angular scores, reversing their ranking contribution. The remaining pipeline is unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same indoor functionality-segmentation task on SceneFun3D split0 and split1. No datasets, domains, or test scenarios are added or removed in the supplement.

E2.justification: OpenMask3D, OpenIns3D, and LERF remain the main comparators. The supplementary comparisons retain the same prompt variants and OpenIns3D configurations using YOLO-World or ODISE, with and without Snap.

E3.justification: The reported experimental settings remain unchanged: 30/200-scene splits, AP/AR and mIoU metrics, the default 50 selected views, score weights, and threshold 0.7. No evaluation protocol or experimental budget is revised.

E4.justification: The architectural ablations, score-weight analysis, view-count/threshold sensitivity, supplementary runtime study, and qualitative success/failure cases are retained without new or removed analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version introduces repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. The existing point estimates and runtime averages retain the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: The main and supplementary numerical results and qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, Tables 1–2 retain Fun3DU mIoU values of 15.2 on split0 and 11.5 on split1. No revised results accompany the score-formula correction.

T1.justification: Equation (2) substantively corrects the mathematical definitions of both distribution scores from KL divergence to one minus KL divergence. This makes larger scores correspond to distributions closer to uniformity, as already intended in the prose. The other definitions and aggregation equations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: a first training-free approach to functionality understanding and segmentation in 3D scenes, with performance exceeding the evaluated open-vocabulary baselines.

C2.justification: Both versions already interpret higher visibility scores as favoring centered, well-visible contextual objects. Explanations of baseline errors, ambiguous descriptions, small-object failures, and applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation and access disclosures are retained, including frozen model components, quantization, hyperparameters, PyTorch, NVIDIA A100 hardware, and project/model/code links. No additional implementation instructions or resource availability changes are reported.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged in both the main paper and supplement. Reference-list movement and changed citation back-reference page numbers do not introduce or remove prior work.

P1.justification: Section 3.4 changes the wording from computing a difference to computing a similarity alongside Equation (2). The arXiv version/date stamps are updated; the narrative and section order otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Equation formatting and spacing change, causing subsequent text to reflow across columns and pages, including the conclusion continuing onto page 9. The figures, tables, captions, and substantive supplementary layout remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Replacing D_KL with 1 - D_KL in Equation (2) removes the contradiction between maximizing the visibility score and preferring distributions closer to uniformity. This improves the mathematical specification of view selection. The experimental evidence and supplementary analyses are unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
